# What's working now — aggregate patterns

**The derived scorecard.** Regenerated by `/ps:post-pulse` after each run from the
records in `posts.jsonl`. The raw data is the source of truth; this file is the
cross-post math on top of it, in plain language, so `/ps:post` can draft *strategy*
(which register, which CTA, how long) without recomputing 47 records mid-draft.

This is not `examples.md`. `examples.md` teaches the **shape** of one good post;
this file teaches **what to write and where the skill's own rules disagree with the
data.** Read both before drafting.

> Regenerated 2026-08-27 (pulse window widened to 2026-07-17→2026-08-27 since the
> last pulse was 41 days ago — the default `week` sweep would have missed a month
> of posts — plus a re-measure pass on the 4 posts from late June/early July still
> due for a refresh). 47 LinkedIn posts, 0 Twitter/X. Signal strength is noted per
> section; cells with n<4 are directional only, never hard rules.

**Baseline:** median engagement rate **2.15%** (avg 2.27%), across 41 posts with
visible impressions. Field-average engagement (reactions+comments+reposts) is **67**.
Anything above ~2% ER / ~67 eng is pulling its weight.

## Pillar — which register to write in (STRONG signal)

| Pillar                | Avg eng | n  | vs field |
|-----------------------|--------:|---:|----------|
| operators-journal     |   82.9  |  9 | +24% ▲   |
| educational-tactical  |   78.6  |  8 | +18% ▲   |
| industry-take         |   69.5  | 13 | +4%      |
| build-in-public       |   50.8  | 17 | −24% ▼   |

→ **RULE, and the inversion is getting worse, not better:** of the 7 posts logged
  since the last pulse, 4 were build-in-public (the weakest pillar) and only 2 were
  operators-journal + 1 educational-tactical (the two strongest). Build-in-public
  now carries 17 of 47 posts — the single largest pillar — while still underperforming
  the field by a quarter. The DR field-conversation posts (operators-journal) keep
  outperforming product-update posts; shift cadence weighting toward them.

## CTA — how to close (STRONG signal)

| CTA                 | Avg eng | n  |
|---------------------|--------:|---:|
| karma-waitlist      |  121.0  |  1 |
| dm-advisory         |   97.6  | 10 |
| github              |   73.0  |  5 |
| (none)              |   55.9  | 19 |
| discord             |   57.0  |  2 |
| engagement-question |   52.0  |  7 |
| newsletter          |   46.3  |  3 |

→ **RULE + CONTRADICTION (held across 3 consecutive pulses now — 07-11, 07-17,
  08-27):** "DM me" keeps beating an engagement-question close by roughly 2×, and a
  bare no-CTA close still edges out engagement-question too. This **contradicts**
  the post skill's standing instruction to always end with an engagement question.
  Three pulses in a row is no longer a fluke — **this pulse formally proposes**
  editing `/ps:post` SKILL.md to stop defaulting to engagement-question and instead
  prefer dm-advisory (especially for Operator's Journal posts) or a clean no-CTA
  close. Pending Pedro's approval; not applied automatically.

## Length (MODERATE signal)

| Bucket          | Avg eng | n  |
|-----------------|--------:|---:|
| 400–800 chars   |   70.8  | 21 |
| <400 chars      |   68.0  | 10 |
| 800–1300+ chars |   61.0  | 16 |

→ **RULE:** Mid-length posts (400–800 chars) remain the strongest bucket, with short
  posts close behind. Long posts (800+) keep trailing both. Still rubs against the
  skill's "700–1,500 typical" LinkedIn default — same contradiction as the last two
  pulses, still not actioned.

## Day of week (WEAK-to-MODERATE signal — cells thickening)

| Day  | Avg eng | n  |
|------|--------:|---:|
| Sun  |   96.4  |  7 |
| Mon  |   72.6  |  9 |
| Sat  |   71.7  |  3 |
| Wed  |   70.7  |  3 |
| Thu  |   64.8  |  5 |
| Fri  |   59.0  | 13 |
| Tue  |   42.3  |  7 |

→ **WATCH:** Thursday's cell grew from n=2 to n=5 this pulse (three new Thu posts),
  and its average dropped from a thin 121 to a more believable 64.8 — a good example
  of why small cells shouldn't be trusted early. Sunday (n=7, unchanged) is still the
  best-supported day and still under-used versus Friday, which remains the most-posted
  day (13) despite a below-field average.

## Outliers worth studying

- **New posts are noisy on first read — same caveat as before.** The brand-new
  `ln-2026-08-27-five-channels-autopilot-test` (1 hour old at capture) shows the
  "highest ER" of the whole dataset (4.8%) purely because it only has 166 impressions
  so far. Treat this as an artifact, not a result, until it's re-measured next pulse.
- **Highest ER with a real sample:** `ln-2026-05-29-vertical-voice-ai-niche` still
  leads at **3.8%** (78 eng / 2,031 imp), with `ln-2026-08-20-dozens-collections-execs-dr`
  (this pulse's strongest genuine new post) close behind at **3.2%** (37 eng / 1,155
  imp) — an operators-journal field-notes post from DR collections executives.
- **Highest reach/eng ever:** unchanged — `ln-2026-01-29` "New adventure. 🚀", 227 eng
  / 8,817 imp.
- **Richest comment thread captured this pulse:** `ln-2026-08-06-rain-changes-collections`
  (8 comments, 3 captured) — a genuine field source thanking Pedro for the
  conversation, another calling the analysis "truly outstanding," and a technical
  question about swapping Twilio for the open-source Somleng in non-US markets. This
  is the kind of qualitative signal the `top_comments` gap has been missing.

## Open questions for the next pulse (data gaps)

- **`top_comments` coverage is improving but still thin.** This pulse captured
  comments for the 2 new posts that had any (rain post: 3 comments; DR-execs post:
  1) rather than trying to backfill older posts. 3/47 records now carry comments in
  their latest snapshot — still worth a dedicated backfill pass at some point.
- **Growth curves are deepening.** 4 posts now have 3+ snapshots (up from 0 last
  pulse) after this run's re-measure pass on the late-June/early-July batch. Not yet
  enough same-post history across 3+ points to say which hooks peak fast vs. slow,
  but the shape is starting to show.
- **Gap risk from the missed cadence:** this pulse had to widen its window to 41
  days to avoid missing posts. If pulses keep slipping past a week, consider running
  `/ps:post-pulse month` on a fixed schedule (e.g. via `/ps:schedule`) rather than
  relying on ad hoc invocation.
- **No Twitter/X data.** All patterns above are LinkedIn-only.

---

### How this file is regenerated

`/ps:post-pulse` recomputes this after each sweep from `posts.jsonl`: averages by
pillar / CTA / length / day-of-week, the ER baseline, the current outliers, and any
place a data pattern contradicts a rule in `/ps:post` (surface those explicitly — they
are the highest-value output; if a contradiction holds across ≥2 pulses, propose the
rule edit for Pedro's approval). Keep it short (~1 screen); it is a summary, not an
archive. Treat every cell with n<4 as directional.
